domain-1.example counts saved cumulative sends per sequence step (step 0 is the first email, step 1 the first follow-up; never say 'step 0' to the customer, say 'first email' and 'first follow-up'); sequenceStepDelays is the configured delay in days on each step. A campaign whose stepSends has only step 0, after its first sends are older than the configured delay, has no saved numeric-step evidence of follow-up sends. Say so plainly: only first emails have been sent and no follow-up has gone out. A dailyMetrics day where emailsSent equals newLeadsContacted means every send that day was a first email. For a question about a whole campaign's follow-ups, answer from these campaign figures before reading any single thread, and do not ask the customer for a prospect name these figures already answer. articles.title: Can I set a per-inbox daily sending limit?
Can I set a per-inbox daily sending limit?

output.content:
There's no user-facing control for daily sending limits. The platform sets the per-inbox daily cap for you based on the inbox's state and how many campaigns it's sending for. You can see the current cap in the Email Accounts table — it's the second number in the **Emails Sent** column (e.g. `12 of 35`).

The maximum cap is **35 campaign emails per inbox per day**. DFY inboxes ramp gradually after warmup until they reach that full capacity. The platform can throttle below 35 when needed, but it never raises an inbox above 35.

## Where to see the current limit

1. **Cold Email Agent** → **Email Accounts**.
2. Scan the **Emails Sent** column. Every row reads `X of Y` where `Y` is today's limit for that inbox.
3. Adjacent columns give you the signal about why the limit is what it is:
   - **Warmup emails** — recent warmup activity count
   - **Health score** — deliverability percentage (aim for 80%+)

## Why it's automatic

Daily limits move in lockstep with three things the platform watches:

| Signal | Effect on daily limit |
|---|---|
| **Warmup duration** | DFY inboxes start lower and ramp up toward 35 after initial warmup |
| **Health score** | A drop in health reduces the daily cap until it recovers |
| **Active campaigns sharing the inbox** | The platform splits the cap across campaigns so one campaign can't starve another |

An Inngest job (`process-daily-email-sent`) recalculates this when campaigns change, inboxes are added/removed, or settings update. The recalculation runs behind the scenes — there's nothing for you to click.

## If the cap feels too low

- **Give it time.** A newly-provisioned DFY inbox ramps gradually after warmup before it reaches the full 35/day capacity.
- **Improve the health score.** If the inbox is landing in spam on warmup, the cap won't rise. Check the warmup folder in Gmail/Outlook and mark any warmup mail as "Not spam."
- **Add more inboxes.** Since limits are per-inbox, additional inboxes linearly raise your total daily send capacity. Buy them in **Cold Email Agent → Email Accounts → Add New Inboxes**.

<Callout title="Don't try to push beyond the cap" type="warning">
Trying to work around the cap damages deliverability. High volume from a cold inbox is the single fastest way to get flagged by Gmail.
</Callout>

## Related

- [Where is the bounce protection toggle for a paused campaign?](/docs/cold-email-agent/faq/campaigns/where-is-the-bounce-protection-toggle-for-a-paused-campaign)
- [Email Accounts](/docs/cold-email-agent/email-accounts)
- [Deliverability concepts](/docs/cold-email-agent/concepts/deliverability)
